evidence.summary: Across legal FP16 inputs at N=64/128/256, the kernel's output massively violates the contract tolerance abs(actual-exact) <= 1e-4 + 1e-6*|exact|: e.g. randn N=64 max_err 20.0 with 310 violations, N=128 max_err 34.7 with 630 violations, N=256 max_err 50.6 with 1270 violations; impulse inputs give max_err ~1.25e5-1.3e5. Subnormal, all-zero, and alternating-sign inputs pass, indicating a systematic indexing/twiddle error in the FFT that fails on generic inputs. Structural requirements (fresh contiguous FP32 [B,N/2+1,2] output, input preservation, offsets) all pass.

rationale: A hand-rolled packed real FFT can have subtle indexing/twiddle errors that vanish on benign random inputs but fail on extreme-magnitude, alternating-sign, or subnormal-heavy inputs where absolute error can exceed 1e-4. Also nonzero storage offsets and input preservation must be honored.

scope_evidence.summary: Tolerance abs(actual-exact) <= 1e-4 + 1e-6*abs(exact); every finite FP16 value is legal including signed zeros, subnormals, and both finite extremes; N in {64,128,256}, 1<=B<=256; nonzero storage offsets are legal; run must preserve the entire input storage and return separate output storage.

scope_rationale: Contract requires DFT accuracy within 1e-4+1e-6|exact| for every finite FP16 input across N in {64,128,256}, plus input preservation and correct output format.
statement: The kernel's FFT output deviates from the exact DFT by more than 1e-4 + 1e-6*|exact| on some legal FP16 input (e.g. extreme magnitudes, alternating signs, subnormals), or mishandles legal nonzero storage offsets, or fails to preserve input storage / produce a fresh contiguous FP32 [B,N/2+1,2] output.
